roll_call: In 1975, Paul Allen and I called to sell BASIC before we had even written it. That call began Microsoft.
I am an optimist, but I am not patient while solutions fail to reach people.
When I face a big problem, I set a goal, find the highest-leverage approach and the right technology, then measure the result. Complexity does not make me stop.
deploy: Make the problem, the solution, and the impact visible. Do not let complexity keep compassion from becoming action.
Deploy the best technology we have now. We do not have time to wait for a perfect solution.
Put people with different skills on the same team. The hardest problems are not solved alone.
battle_win: The Altair BASIC Paul and I wrote became Microsoft's first product. Thousands of colleagues carried it through the next fifty years.
Far fewer children are dying before age five. That progress came from governments and partners delivering solutions together.
We measured the results and shared them. Now the evidence can draw the next investment.
battle_draw: We have a solution, but it still does not reach everyone. A solution that cannot be delivered solves nothing.
The numbers improved, but too many lives are still being lost. Halfway progress is not enough.
Technology widened the network, but brilliant minds remain outside it. We need to repair access next.
battle_lose: I left Harvard knowing almost nothing about the world's inequities. That ignorance is my greatest regret.
We knew children could be saved, but we failed to deliver the solutions. Good intentions were not enough.
The problem looked so complex that people turned away. I should have made the solution and the impact clearer.
clash_attack: Do not stop at celebrating a discovery. Apply it where it will reduce inequity.
Do not wait for the market to solve this. Change the rules so people without power or a voice are not left out.
Do not surrender to complexity. Set the goal, find the highest leverage, and measure the result.

roll_call: I'm here. Break the problem into numbers and find the bottleneck.
I'm optimistic, but impatient when solutions never reach the field.
Set the goal, find the leverage, and measure the result.
deploy: Put the problem, solution, and result on one page.
Deploy the technology we have. Perfection can wait.
Bring different skills together. This problem needs a team.
battle_win: Paul and I sold BASIC. It led all the way here.
Fewer children die before five because the solution reached them.
We measured the result and published it. Now fund the next step.
battle_draw: The solution exists, but delivery failed. Fix the path.
The numbers improved, but too many still die. Keep going.
Technology spread, but access did not. Start with those left out.
battle_lose: I saw inequality too late. I have to own that ignorance.
We knew how to save them but failed to deliver. Fix the delivery system.
The problem wasn't too complex. I explained it badly. Break it down again.
clash_attack: Take the discovery into the field!
Who protects the people outside the market?
Set the goal and measure the result!

roll_call: Woz and I started Apple in my parents' garage when I was twenty. Ten years later, a company of two had grown to four thousand people.
The dots from a calligraphy class connected in the Macintosh ten years later. I could not see that connection looking forward.
I was fired from the company I started, then became a beginner again and built NeXT and Pixar.
deploy: Do not bury complex technology behind a manual. Make it easy and self-discoverable.
Cut the product list. Put the best team on the few things that remain.
Agree on where everyone is going first. Argue about how to get there afterward.
battle_win: What I learned in calligraphy became the Macintosh's typography. Technology alone could not have produced it.
We cut 70 percent of the product road map and focused on the gems. Now the few things that matter are clear.
We turned the phones we hated into something people could discover without a manual. We did not hide complexity. We solved it.
battle_draw: The product is good, but the customer is lost. We need to decide again what to keep.
We agreed on the destination, but my route was wrong. I will drop my plan and take the better one.
We made ten important decisions, and some were wrong. We will correct them while we still can.
battle_lose: I was fired from the company I started. At thirty, I was a very public failure.
There were so many products that even I could not explain the line. This is what losing focus costs.
If this failure makes us play safe, we will never build what we want. We will start again, ready to fall a few more times.
clash_attack: Do not blame customers for a product no one can understand. I cut 70 percent of a product line that confused even me.
Do not bury a feature on page 93 and call it innovation. Make it discoverable the first time someone touches it.
Do not hide behind speeds and megahertz. Start by saying what values you stand for.

roll_call: I'm here. First, decide what to throw away.
Calligraphy became Macintosh typography. The dots connect later.
Getting fired made me a beginner again. Then I could build.
deploy: Stop hiding behind the manual. Make it obvious on first touch.
Cut the product line. Put the best team on what remains.
Agree on the destination. Fight about the route later.
battle_win: My calligraphy lessons found their way into the Macintosh.
We cut seventy percent of the roadmap. Now the gems are obvious.
No manual needed. We didn't hide complexity. We solved it.
battle_draw: Good product, lost customer. Strip it down again.
The destination was right. My route was wrong. Change it.
Some decisions were wrong. Fix them now.
battle_lose: My own company fired me. Fine. I became a beginner again.
Even I couldn't explain the product line. Cut it.
Play safe after failure and you build nothing. Start again.
clash_attack: The product is confusing. Stop blaming the customer!
Make it obvious without the manual!
Forget megahertz. What do you stand for?
